title: Python Conditional Logic
description: Trace if, elif, and else branches. These questions focus on choosing the correct branch, not on syntax memorization alone.

questions.prompt: Which branch runs when an if condition is false and the next condition is true?
questions.explanation: elif means else if: Python checks it after the earlier if condition fails.
84 is not greater than 89 but is greater than 79, so the elif branch assigns B.

questions.prompt: An else branch runs only when every preceding if or elif condition is false.
questions.explanation: else is the fallback branch after all earlier conditions have failed.

questions.prompt: Which operator tests whether two values are equal?
questions.explanation: == compares values. A single = assigns a value to a name.
68 is not at least 70, so the else branch prints cool.

questions.prompt: Why is the order of grade conditions important?
options: The first true branch is the one Python uses
Python checks every branch after the first match
The final else branch is checked before the conditions
Reordering conditions changes the type of the score
questions.correct: The first true branch is the one Python uses
questions.explanation: Once an if or elif condition is true, Python skips the remaining branches in that chain.
-2 is neither greater than zero nor equal to zero, so the fallback branch runs.

questions.prompt: Indentation tells Python which statements belong to a conditional branch.
questions.explanation: The indented block after the colon is the code controlled by that condition.
<= means less than or equal to, and 5 is equal to 5.
An empty list is falsy in a condition, so the else branch runs.
